# Purpose

Annual Kobe probabilities can be read from the Stock Synthesis delta-method
covariance. Under the multivariate lognormal approximation,

$$
\left(\log(B/B_{MSY}), \log(F/F_{MSY})\right)
$$

is bivariate normal, so the four quadrant probabilities are values of the
bivariate normal cdf. They do not need a new Monte Carlo. A Monte Carlo from
the same mean and covariance, as in `ssmvln()`, is only a check: the two
answers should differ by Monte Carlo error.

This replaces an earlier note that swapped the yellow and orange quadrants.
The names below match `kobe.R` and `kobeGreen()`.

| Quadrant | Stock | Fishing | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| green | \(B/B_{MSY} > 1\) | \(F/F_{MSY} < 1\) | not overfished, no overfishing |
| orange | \(B/B_{MSY} > 1\) | \(F/F_{MSY} > 1\) | overfishing only |
| yellow | \(B/B_{MSY} < 1\) | \(F/F_{MSY} < 1\) | overfished only |
| red | \(B/B_{MSY} < 1\) | \(F/F_{MSY} > 1\) | overfished and overfishing |

# A self-contained year

The moments below are the 2026 North Atlantic shortfin mako terminal year
used in the `kobeGreen()` example. Log-scale means are `log` of the point
estimates, because the SS3 estimate is treated as the median.

```{r quadrants}
muB <- log(0.95)
muF <- log(0.72)
sigmaB <- 0.174
sigmaF <- 0.384
rho <- -0.652

Sigma <- matrix(c(sigmaB^2, rho * sigmaB * sigmaF,
                  rho * sigmaB * sigmaF, sigmaF^2), 2, 2)

quadrant <- function(lower, upper) {
  if (!requireNamespace("mvtnorm", quietly = TRUE))
    return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(mvtnorm::pmvnorm(lower = lower, upper = upper,
                              mean = c(muB, muF), sigma = Sigma))
}

probs <- c(
  green  = quadrant(c(0, -Inf), c(Inf, 0)),
  orange = quadrant(c(0, 0),    c(Inf, Inf)),
  yellow = quadrant(c(-Inf, -Inf), c(0, 0)),
  red    = quadrant(c(-Inf, 0), c(0, Inf))
)
round(probs, 3)
round(sum(probs), 6)
```

The four probabilities sum to one. Marginal checks use the univariate normal
on the log scale: \(P(B > B_{MSY}) = 1 - \Phi(0; \mu_B, \sigma_B)\) and
\(P(F < F_{MSY}) = \Phi(0; \mu_F, \sigma_F)\).

The same calculation is written as `kobeGreen()` and `kobeProbs()` in
`kobeAnalytic.R` from the shortfin-mako code drop. That file is not yet in
`R/`, so those names are not exported. `kobeProbs(dq, covar, year)` builds
the moments from `derived_quants` and `CoVar`. `transform = "current"` copies
`ssmvln()`, which sets the log-scale correlation equal to the natural-scale
correlation. `"exact"` uses \(\log(1 + \rho\, CV_u CV_v)\).

# From an SS3 run

`Bratio_YYYY` and `F_YYYY` are \(B/B_{MSY}\) and \(F/F_{MSY}\) only when
`starter.ss` sets the depletion basis to \(SSB_{MSY}\) and `F_std_scaling` to
\(F/F_{MSY}\).

```{r ss3, eval=FALSE}
library(r4ss)
library(FLRebuild)

ss <- SS_output("path/to/run")
kobeProbs(ss$derived_quants, ss$CoVar, 2024)

# Monte Carlo from the same MVLN, for comparison
sim <- ssmvln(ss$CoVar, ss$derived_quants, mc = 10000)
```

For a grid of future catches, `kobeMomentGrid()` stacks one `SS_output` per
catch level. `kobeRebuildTime()` interpolates the year at which the green
probability crosses a target (0.60 to 0.70 for North Atlantic shortfin mako
under Recommendation 21-09). That year is not a biomass rebuilding time.
`rebuildTime()` answers the biomass question.

# What this does not replace

The analytic probabilities are the deterministic form of the MVLN, not a
closed-loop test of a harvest rule. Use them for the Kobe status of a fitted
run and for a Kobe II matrix across catch levels that share one forecast
specification. Use `rebuild()` when the question is the trajectory of biomass.
